T1003.001.subject: C0014
T1003.001.text: During Operation Wocao, threat actors used ProcDump to dump credentials from memory.

T1003.001.subject: C0025
T1003.001.text: During the 2016 Ukraine Electric Power Attack, Sandworm Team used Mimikatz to capture and use legitimate credentials.

T1003.001.subject: C0029
T1003.001.text: During Cutting Edge, threat actors used Task Manager to dump LSASS memory from Windows devices to disk.

T1003.001.subject: C0030
T1003.001.text: In the Triton Safety Instrumented System Attack, TEMP.Veles used Mimikatz.

T1003.001.subject: C0032
T1003.001.text: During the C0032 campaign, TEMP.Veles used Mimikatz and a custom tool, SecHack, to harvest credentials.

T1003.001.subject: C0038
T1003.001.text: During HomeLand Justice, threat actors dumped LSASS memory on compromised hosts.

T1003.001.subject: C0058
T1003.001.text: During SharePoint ToolShell Exploitation, threat actors used Mimikatz to dump LSASS memory.

T1003.001.subject: C0061
T1003.001.text: During Operation Digital Eye, threat actors targeted memory from the LSASS process to extract credentials.

T1003.001.subject: C0063
T1003.001.text: During the 2025 Poland Wiper Attacks, the adversaries attempted to dump credentials utilizing LSASS.

T1003.001.subject: G0003
T1003.001.text: Cleaver has been known to dump credentials using Mimikatz and Windows Credential Editor.

T1003.001.subject: G0004
T1003.001.text: Ke3chang has dumped credentials, including by using Mimikatz.

T1003.001.subject: G0006
T1003.001.text: APT1 has been known to use credential dumping using Mimikatz.

T1003.001.subject: G0007
T1003.001.text: APT28 regularly deploys both publicly available (ex: Mimikatz) and custom password retrieval tools on victims. They have also dumped the LSASS process memory using the MiniDump function.

T1003.001.subject: G0022
T1003.001.text: APT3 has used a tool to dump credentials by injecting itself into lsass.exe and triggering with the argument "dig."

T1003.001.subject: G0027
T1003.001.text: Threat Group-3390 actors have used a modified version of Mimikatz called Wrapikatz to dump credentials. They have also dumped credentials from domain controllers.

T1003.001.subject: G0034
T1003.001.text: Sandworm Team has used its plainpwd tool, a modified version of Mimikatz, and comsvcs.dll to dump Windows credentials from system memory.

T1003.001.subject: G0037
T1003.001.text: FIN6 has used Windows Credential Editor for credential dumping.

T1003.001.subject: G0049
T1003.001.text: OilRig has used credential dumping tools such as Mimikatz to steal credentials to accounts logged into the compromised system and to Outlook Web Access.

T1003.001.subject: G0050
T1003.001.text: APT32 used Mimikatz and customized versions of Windows Credential Dumper to harvest credentials.

T1003.001.subject: G0059
T1003.001.text: Magic Hound has stolen domain credentials by dumping LSASS process memory using Task Manager, comsvcs.dll, and from a Microsoft Active Directory Domain Controller using Mimikatz.

T1003.001.subject: G0060
T1003.001.text: BRONZE BUTLER has used various tools (such as Mimikatz and WCE) to perform credential dumping.

T1003.001.subject: G0061
T1003.001.text: FIN8 harvests credentials using Invoke-Mimikatz or Windows Credentials Editor (WCE).

T1003.001.subject: G0064
T1003.001.text: APT33 has used a variety of publicly available tools like LaZagne, Mimikatz, and ProcDump to dump credentials.

T1003.001.subject: G0065
T1003.001.text: Leviathan has used publicly available tools to dump password hashes, including ProcDump and WCE.

T1003.001.subject: G0068
T1003.001.text: PLATINUM has used keyloggers that are also capable of dumping credentials.

T1003.001.subject: G0069
T1003.001.text: MuddyWater has performed credential dumping with Mimikatz and procdump64.exe.

T1003.001.subject: G0077
T1003.001.text: Leafminer used several tools for retrieving login and password information, including LaZagne and Mimikatz.

T1003.001.subject: G0087
T1003.001.text: APT39 has used Mimikatz, Windows Credential Editor and ProcDump to dump credentials.

T1003.001.subject: G0091
T1003.001.text: Silence has used the Farse6.1 utility (based on Mimikatz) to extract credentials from lsass.exe.

T1003.001.subject: G0093
T1003.001.text: GALLIUM used a modified version of Mimikatz along with a PowerShell-based Mimikatz to dump credentials on the victim machines.

T1003.001.subject: G0094
T1003.001.text: Kimsuky has gathered credentials using Mimikatz and ProcDump.

T1003.001.subject: G0096
T1003.001.text: APT41 has used hashdump, Mimikatz, Procdump, and the Windows Credential Editor to dump password hashes from memory and authenticate to other user accounts.

T1003.001.subject: G0102
T1003.001.text: Wizard Spider has dumped the lsass.exe memory to harvest credentials with the use of open-source tool LaZagne.

T1003.001.subject: G0107
T1003.001.text: Whitefly has used Mimikatz to obtain credentials.

T1003.001.subject: G0108
T1003.001.text: Blue Mockingbird has used Mimikatz to retrieve credentials from LSASS memory.

T1003.001.subject: G0117
T1003.001.text: Fox Kitten has used prodump to dump credentials from LSASS.

T1003.001.subject: G0119
T1003.001.text: Indrik Spider used Cobalt Strike to carry out credential dumping using ProcDump.

T1003.001.subject: G0125
T1003.001.text: HAFNIUM has used procdump to dump the LSASS process memory.

T1003.001.subject: G0129
T1003.001.text: Mustang Panda has harvested credentials from memory of lssas.exe with Mimikatz.

T1003.001.subject: G0143
T1003.001.text: Aquatic Panda has attempted to harvest credentials through LSASS memory dumping.

T1003.001.subject: G1003
T1003.001.text: Ember Bear uses legitimate Sysinternals tools such as procdump to dump LSASS memory.

T1003.001.subject: G1006
T1003.001.text: Earth Lusca has used ProcDump to obtain the hashes of credentials by dumping the memory of the LSASS process.

T1003.001.subject: G1016
T1003.001.text: FIN13 has obtained memory dumps with ProcDump to parse and extract credentials from a victim's LSASS process memory with Mimikatz.

T1003.001.subject: G1017
T1003.001.text: Volt Typhoon has attempted to access hashed credentials from the LSASS process memory space.

T1003.001.subject: G1023
T1003.001.text: APT5 has used the Task Manager process to target LSASS process memory in order to obtain NTLM password hashes. APT5 has also dumped clear text passwords and hashes from memory using Mimikatz hosted through an RDP mapped drive.

T1003.001.subject: G1030
T1003.001.text: Agrius used tools such as Mimikatz to dump LSASS memory to capture credentials in victim environments.

T1003.001.subject: G1036
T1003.001.text: Moonstone Sleet retrieved credentials from LSASS memory.

T1003.001.subject: G1039
T1003.001.text: RedCurl used LaZagne to obtain passwords from memory.

T1003.001.subject: G1040
T1003.001.text: Play has used Mimikatz and the Windows Task Manager to dump LSASS process memory.

T1003.001.subject: G1048
T1003.001.text: UNC3886 has used MiniDump to dump process memory and search for cleartext credentials.

T1003.001.subject: G1051
T1003.001.text: Medusa Group has leveraged Mimikatz to dump LSASS to harvest credentials.

T1003.001.subject: G1054
T1003.001.text: MirrorFace has dumped LSASS memory for credential access.

T1003.001.subject: G1055
T1003.001.text: VOID MANTICORE has dumped LSASS credentials using `comsvcs.dll` via `rundll32.exe`.

T1003.001.subject: S0002
T1003.001.text: Mimikatz performs credential dumping to obtain account and password information useful in gaining access to additional systems and enterprise network resources. It contains functionality to acquire information about credentials in many ways, including from the LSASS Memory.

T1003.001.subject: S0005
T1003.001.text: Windows Credential Editor can dump credentials.

T1003.001.subject: S0046
T1003.001.text: CozyCar has executed Mimikatz to harvest stored credentials from the victim and further victim penetration.

T1003.001.subject: S0056
T1003.001.text: Net Crawler uses credential dumpers such as Mimikatz and Windows Credential Editor to extract cached credentials from Windows systems.

T1003.001.subject: S0121
T1003.001.text: Lslsass can dump active logon session password hashes from the lsass process.

T1003.001.subject: S0154
T1003.001.text: Cobalt Strike can spawn a job to inject into LSASS memory and dump password hashes.

T1003.001.subject: S0187
T1003.001.text: Daserf leverages Mimikatz and Windows Credential Editor to steal credentials.

T1003.001.subject: S0192
T1003.001.text: Pupy can execute Lazagne as well as Mimikatz using PowerShell.

T1003.001.subject: S0194
T1003.001.text: PowerSploit contains a collection of Exfiltration modules that can harvest credentials using Mimikatz.

T1003.001.subject: S0342
T1003.001.text: GreyEnergy has a module for Mimikatz to collect Windows credentials from the victim’s machine.

T1003.001.subject: S0349
T1003.001.text: LaZagne can perform credential dumping from memory to obtain account and password information.

T1003.001.subject: S0357
T1003.001.text: SecretsDump and Mimikatz modules within Impacket can perform credential dumping to obtain account and password information.

T1003.001.subject: S0363
T1003.001.text: Empire contains an implementation of Mimikatz to gather credentials from memory.

T1003.001.subject: S0365
T1003.001.text: Olympic Destroyer contains a module that tries to obtain credentials from LSASS, similar to Mimikatz. These credentials are used with PsExec and Windows Management Instrumentation to help the malware propagate itself across a network.

T1003.001.subject: S0367
T1003.001.text: Emotet has been observed dropping and executing password grabber modules including Mimikatz.

T1003.001.subject: S0368
T1003.001.text: NotPetya contains a modified version of Mimikatz to help gather credentials that are later used for lateral movement.

T1003.001.subject: S0378
T1003.001.text: PoshC2 contains an implementation of Mimikatz to gather credentials from memory.

T1003.001.subject: S0428
T1003.001.text: PoetRAT used voStro.exe, a compiled pypykatz (Python version of Mimikatz), to steal credentials.

T1003.001.subject: S0439
T1003.001.text: Okrum was seen using MimikatzLite to perform credential dumping.

T1003.001.subject: S0583
T1003.001.text: Pysa can perform OS credential dumping using Mimikatz.

T1003.001.subject: S0606
T1003.001.text: Bad Rabbit has used Mimikatz to harvest credentials from the victim's machine.

T1003.001.subject: S0633
T1003.001.text: Sliver has a built-in `procdump` command allowing for retrieval of memory from processes such as `lsass.exe` for credential harvesting.

T1003.001.subject: S0681
T1003.001.text: Lizar can run Mimikatz to harvest credentials.

T1003.001.subject: S0692
T1003.001.text: SILENTTRINITY can create a memory dump of LSASS via the `MiniDumpWriteDump Win32` API call.

T1003.001.subject: S1060
T1003.001.text: Mafalda can dump password hashes from `LSASS.exe`.

T1003.001.subject: S1242
T1003.001.text: Qilin can employ an embedded Mimikatz module to dump LSASS memory.

T1003.002.subject: C0002
T1003.002.text: During Night Dragon, threat actors dumped account hashes using gsecdump.

T1003.002.subject: C0012
T1003.002.text: During Operation CuckooBees, the threat actors leveraged a custom tool to dump OS credentials and used following commands: `reg save HKLM\\SYSTEM system.hiv`, `reg save HKLM\\SAM sam.hiv`, and `reg save HKLM\\SECURITY security.hiv`, to dump SAM, SYSTEM and SECURITY hives.

T1003.002.subject: C0017
T1003.002.text: During C0017, APT41 copied the `SAM` and `SYSTEM` Registry hives for credential harvesting.

T1003.002.subject: C0041
T1003.002.text: During FrostyGoop Incident, the adversary retrieved the contents of the Security Account Manager (SAM) hive in the victim environment for credential capture.

T1003.002.subject: C0051
T1003.002.text: During APT28 Nearest Neighbor Campaign, APT28 used the following commands to dump SAM, SYSTEM, and SECURITY hives: reg save hklm\sam, reg save hklm\system, and reg save hklm\security.

T1003.002.subject: C0061
T1003.002.text: During Operation Digital Eye, threat actors used `reg save` to retrieve credentials from the Security Account Manager (SAM) database.

T1003.002.subject: C0063
T1003.002.text: During the 2025 Poland Wiper Attacks, the adversaries had stolen Security Account Manager (SAM) and SYSTEM registry hives.

T1003.002.text: APT29 has used the `reg save` command to save registry hives.

T1003.002.text: Threat Group-3390 actors have used gsecdump to dump credentials. They have also dumped credentials from domain controllers.

T1003.002.subject: G0035
T1003.002.text: Dragonfly has dropped and executed SecretsDump to dump password hashes.

T1003.002.subject: G0045
T1003.002.text: menuPass has used a modified version of pentesting tools wmiexec.vbs and secretsdump.py to dump credentials.

T1003.002.subject: G0093
T1003.002.text: GALLIUM used reg commands to dump specific hives from the Windows Registry, such as the SAM hive, and obtain password hashes.

T1003.002.subject: G0102
T1003.002.text: Wizard Spider has acquired credentials from the SAM/SECURITY registry hives.

T1003.002.text: Ember Bear acquires victim credentials by extracting registry hives such as the Security Account Manager through commands such as reg save.

T1003.002.text: FIN13 has extracted the SAM and SYSTEM registry hives using the `reg.exe` binary for obtaining password hashes from a compromised machine.

T1003.002.subject: G1023
T1003.002.text: APT5 has copied and exfiltrated the SAM Registry hive from targeted systems.

T1003.002.subject: G1030
T1003.002.text: Agrius dumped the SAM file on victim machines to capture credentials.

T1003.002.subject: G1034
T1003.002.text: Daggerfly used Reg to dump the Security Account Manager (SAM) hive from victim machines for follow-on credential extraction.

T1003.002.text: MirrorFace has used vssadmin to copy registry hives including SAM.

T1003.002.text: Mivast has the capability to gather NTLM password information.

T1003.002.text: Fgdump can dump Windows password hashes.

T1003.002.text: Cobalt Strike can recover hashed passwords.

T1003.003.text: During Cutting Edge, threat actors accessed and mounted virtual hard disk backups to extract ntds.dit.

T1003.003.text: During Operation MidnightEclipse, threat actors obtained active directory credentials via the NTDS.DIT file.

T1003.003.text: During APT28 Nearest Neighbor Campaign, APT28 dumped NTDS.dit through creating volume shadow copies via vssadmin.

T1003.003.text: Ke3chang has used NTDSDump and other password dumping tools to gather credentials.

T1003.003.text: Sandworm Team has used `ntdsutil.exe` to back up the Active Directory database, likely for credential access.

T1003.003.text: Dragonfly has dropped and executed SecretsDump to dump password hashes. They also obtained ntds.dit from domain controllers.

T1003.003.subject: G0045

T1003.003.text: APT41 used ntdsutil to obtain a copy of the victim environment ntds.dit file.

T1003.003.subject: G0102

T1003.003.subject: G0114
T1003.003.text: Chimera has gathered the SYSTEM registry and ntds.dit files from target systems. T1098.002.text: Magic Hound granted compromised email accounts read access to the email boxes of additional targeted accounts. T1485.subject: S0659

T1485.subject: S0688

T1485.subject: S1135
T1485.text: MultiLayer Wiper deletes files on network drives, but corrupts and overwrites with random data files stored locally.

T1485.subject: S1167

T1485.subject: S9030

T1485.subject: S9039
